newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peronists take lead in Argentine province - survey.
newsitem.headline: Peronists take lead in Argentine province - survey.

text.p: The ruling Peronists have gained a slight edge in popularity over the center-left Frepaso in Buenos Aires province ahead of October mid-term elections, according to a poll Monday in the Clarin newspaper.
But in the city of Buenos Aires, a traditional stronghold of the Radical Party, the Frepaso candidate was in the lead, the survey by Centro de Estudios de Opinion Publica showed.
Argentina renews half of its 257-seat Lower House of Congress in October.
Two women are separately leading the Peronist versus Frepaso slates in Buenos Aires province, home to 40 percent of the country's voters.
Peronist Hilda "Chiche" Duhalde, wife of governor and presidential hopeful Eduardo Duhalde, has overtaken Frepaso senator Graciela Fernandez Meijide by 34 percent to 30 percent, the poll showed.
Duhalde was more popular than her Peronist Party in Buenos Aires province, where the Peronists led Frepaso 24.1 percent to 19.3 percent, according to the May 5-13 survey of 1,046 people.

The Radical party trailed in third place with 16 percent support for its lead candidate, former President Raul Alfonsin, and 13.3 percent for the party, according the poll, which had a margin of error of plus or minus 2.25 percent.

In Buenos Aires city, Frepaso leader Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez was led Radical leader Rodolfo Terragno 32.5 percent to 21.5 percent while as a party Frepaso was ahead with 31.2 percent against 15.5 percent for the Radicals.
The Peronist candidate, speedboat racer Daniel Scioli who was handpicked by President Carlos Menem, lagged far behind with 8.9 percent support while his party had 12.9 percent support.
Survey respondents in both voting districts said their main concerns were unemployment (66.9 percent), low wages (63.8 percent) and corruption (61 percent).
